# Portcullis — File Formats (v0.1)

Three files may live in a repository. **None of them is read in untrusted mode** unless
passed explicitly from outside the scan root (REQUIREMENTS FR-40).

## 1. `context.lock`

Line-based, diff-friendly, no external parser needed. Modelled on `go.sum`.

```
# context.lock — generated by portcullis; review changes to this file like code.
portcullis-lock 1
ruleset 2026.10.0
forced false
sha256:6f1ed002ab5595859014ebf0951522d9f2b8f6c1a8d1e3c7c3d5a5b7b6f2e8a1  .claude/settings.json
sha256:3b1c4f3e2d0a9b8c7d6e5f4a3b2c1d0e9f8a7b6c5d4e3f2a1b0c9d8e7f6a5b4c  CLAUDE.md
sha256:…  "docs/odd\tname/AGENTS.md"
```

Rules:

- Line 1 comment is fixed; `portcullis-lock 1` is the format version; unknown versions ⇒ exit `2`.
- `forced true` when `portcullis lock --force` approved content that had findings ≥ threshold.
- Entries: `sha256:<64 hex>`, two spaces, path. Paths are relative, `/`-separated, sorted
  byte-wise. A path containing control characters, a leading/trailing space or starting
  with `"` is written Go-quoted (`strconv.Quote`).
- Hash input = file bytes with every `\r\n` replaced by `\n` (FR-51). No other normalisation —
  invisible characters, BOMs and encoding changes all change the hash.
- Any malformed line ⇒ exit `2` (a tampered lock never "passes").

## 2. `.portcullis.yaml` (configuration)

Read from the user config directory, `--config`, or — trusted mode only — the scan root
(or `--base-snapshot`). Decoded strictly (unknown keys are errors).

```yaml
version: 1
fail_on: high                 # info | low | medium | high | critical | none
max_file_size: 10MiB
exclude:                      # directories not descended (targets inside still counted)
  - third_party/**
rules:
  disable: [PCL-AEX-001]      # rule IDs; disabling a critical rule prints a warning
  severity:                   # per-rule overrides
    PCL-AEX-002: medium
  dirs: [tools/portcullis-rules]   # extra rule directories
```

## 3. `.portcullis-baseline.yaml` (suppressions)

Accepted known findings, keyed by fingerprint. Every entry needs a reason; entries whose
fingerprint no longer matches anything are reported as stale (`info`) so the file shrinks over time.

```yaml
version: 1
suppressions:
  - fingerprint: 9f2c4e1a0b7d3c6e8f5a2b1c0d9e8f7a
    rule: PCL-AEX-003
    path: package.json
    reason: "prepare script only runs husky install; reviewed 2026-10-13 by @cemilalp02"
```

`rule` and `path` are informational (for review); matching is by fingerprint only.
